question: Federal District Senate Election: 2nd Place
resolution_criteria:
The Brazilian Federal Senate election for Federal District is scheduled to take place on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the second-most valid votes of any candidate at the specified election.

Candidates will be primarily ranked by order of valid votes won. If two or more candidates are tied for any position, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates’ listed full names as they appear in this market. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the second-highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., www.tse.jus.br/eleicoes/resultados-eleicoes).

"Other" means any option not listed here.

# Federal District Senate 2026: who finishes 2nd

## 1. Resolution source
- The official source is the TSE results portal (www.tse.jus.br/eleicoes/resultados-eleicoes). I did not fetch it; before October 4 it would show no results for this race.
- Two seats are up in the Federal District (DF). Each voter picks two names, and the two candidates with the most votes win. This market pays on whoever has the second-most valid votes.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settled the race by October 1. Most polls put Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) first. Second place is a close fight between Leila do Vôlei (PDT, the incumbent), Bia Kicis (PL) and Erika Kokay (PT).
- 2026-09-29: Ronaldo Fonseca (PSD) dropped out on September 28, according to Carta Capital. [CartaCapital](https://www.cartacapital.com.br/politica/michelle-lidera-disputa-ao-senado-no-df-aponta-real-time-big-data/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-29: **Quaest** (fieldwork Sep 25-28, 1,104 voters). Counting both votes: Michelle 26%, Leila 20%, Kicis 18%, Kokay 16%. Sebastião Coelho (Novo), Fonseca, Guilherme Amorim and Zanata 1% each. Guto Felício dos Santos and David Horn 0%. First vote only: Michelle 42%, Kokay 20%, Leila 18%, Kicis 8%. Kicis is weak as a first choice, so her support depends on Michelle voters giving her their second vote. [DGABC](https://www.dgabc.com.br/Noticia/4349819/quaest-no-distrito-federal-michelle-tem-26-para-o-senado-leila-20-bia-18-erika-16)
- 2026-09-29: **Real Time Big Data** (Sep 24-28, 1,600 voters, margin ±2). Michelle 27%, Leila 18%, Kicis 18%, Kokay 16%, Coelho 11%, Guto Felício 1%. The source says this is a technical tie for second. [CartaCapital](https://www.cartacapital.com.br/politica/michelle-lidera-disputa-ao-senado-no-df-aponta-real-time-big-data/)

- 2026-09-23: **Quaest**: Michelle 26%, Leila 19%, Kokay 15%, Kicis 15%. [DGABC](https://www.dgabc.com.br/Noticia/4348728/michelle-tem-26-para-o-senado-do-df-leila-19-erika-e-bia-15)
- 2026-09-14/16: **Datafolha** (Sep 8-10, 910 voters, ±3). Michelle 21%, Leila 18%, Kicis 15%, Kokay 14%. Coelho, Amorim and Fonseca 2% each. Guto Felício, Avenir Rosa and David Horn 1% each. Blank or null 11%, undecided 9%. In August Datafolha had Michelle 19%, Leila 16%, Kokay 12%, Kicis 11%, so Kicis was gaining. [Brasil de Fato](https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/09/16/pesquisa-datafolha-aponta-empate-tecnico-na-segunda-vaga-para-o-senado-no-df/)
- 2026-09-08: **Quaest** reported a technical tie for the second seat. [Brasil de Fato](https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/09/08/pesquisa-quaest-aponta-empate-tecnico-na-segunda-vaga-para-o-senado-no-df/)
- 2026-09-03: A column said the gap between Kicis and Leila in Quaest was shrinking. [O Hoje](https://ohoje.com/coluna/bia-kicis-assusta-esquerda-do-df-na-disputa-ao-senado/)
- Early August 2026: the PL named Michelle and Kicis as its two Senate candidates, both backed by Bolsonaro. [Poder360](https://www.poder360.com.br/poder-eleicoes/bolsonaro-indica-michelle-e-bia-kicis-para-o-senado-no-df-pelo-pl/)
- Several polls were released after October 1. I left them out because they fall past the cutoff.

## 4. Base rates
- The DF has leaned right in recent Senate races. In 2018, the last two-seat race, Leila (then PSB) and Izalci (PSDB) won. In 2022 Damares Alves won the single seat. This is from my own background knowledge; I did not check it with a source.
- Trend through September: Michelle led every poll I found. Leila was usually second, but her lead over Kicis shrank from about 3-5 points to 0-2 points. Kokay was 2-4 points behind the second-place candidate. With error margins of ±2 to 3 points, second place is a statistical toss-up between Leila and Kicis, with Kokay still in range.
- The minor listed candidates (Avenir Rosa, David Horn, Guto Felício dos Santos) poll at 0-1%. The one notable unlisted candidate is Sebastião Coelho (Novo), at 1-2% in most polls but 11% in Real Time Big Data. He would count as "Other".

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold page or prices for this market. I found no published expert forecasts either.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Final polls from Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel are expected in the last days before the vote, plus any last campaign events.
- 2026-10-04: election day. TSE results normally come out the same evening.
- Things that could decide second place:
  - how many Michelle voters give their second vote to Kicis;
  - whether left-leaning voters split between Leila and Kokay or vote tactically;
  - Fonseca's withdrawal.
